To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Re:** Departures from the Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback

## Headline view

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" against our playbook – it is a seller-favourable draft on almost every limitation point, and the Disclosure Letter is actually more candid than the Seller Update: it confirms that several items the Update describes as "addressed" or "adequate" are, in fact, open (Bluefen consent not obtained, Riverlark not repaid, bonuses not in funds flow, Ironquay payment unverified). Where the two documents conflict, the Disclosure Letter's facts should be treated as the current record and the Update's characterisations should not be accepted.

Note on authority: two Seller numbers (20% / AUD 4.8m cap; 18-month claims period) happen to match our *conditional* fallbacks. Under playbook 0.4/6.3 that is not clearance. No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for either, so our stated position remains 25% / AUD 6m and 24 months.

---

## 1. Liability limitations

| Point | Seller | Playbook | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority | Not authorised. Hold at 25%. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar (tipping)** | 5x our figure and the wrong mechanic. The excess-only ("deductible") structure means the first AUD 250k of loss is never recoverable. |
| Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost approval (none) | Not authorised. Hold at 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Default sweep | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reverses the burden – every carve-out would have to be fought for individually. Must be deleted; the default should be that limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |

**Pushback:** reject 12.1–12.3 as drafted; re-propose 25%/AUD 6m, AUD 5k/AUD 50k tipping basket, 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.

## 2. Fundamental/Title warranties collapsed into the general regime

Seller proposes capacity and title warranties share general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is the most significant structural departure. On a 100%-share acquisition, title and capacity are the foundation of the deal; if the Seller does not own the shares, a 20% cap is meaningless.

**Pushback:** separate Fundamental Warranty regime – cap at 100% of price, minimum six-year period, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier. Non-negotiable per playbook.

## 3. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"

Taken literally this captures fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct, Tax, IP, the Ironquay specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims. There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Update.

**Pushback:** express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to the maximum extent enforceable. Specific indemnities, Tax, IP, Title, payment obligations and covenants to sit in their own regimes. No one on our side has authority to concede this.

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

Seller relies on whole-data-room disclosure (everything in the VDR as at 22 Sept 2026, DD-002 to DD-012) plus statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

**Pushback:** specific, fair disclosure only – facts disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete general data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. We can accept the Disclosure Letter's specific paragraphs 2–10 as the starting point for what is actually disclosed, but note that para 1.4 (nothing admits that any consent/payment/notice is "legally required") means the Seller is not disclosing conclusions, only documents – so the disclosure protects them without informing us.

## 5. Clause 8.3 – blanket buyer knowledge exclusion

"No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." Combined with general disclosure, this would effectively eliminate the warranty package: anything in the VDR is both "disclosed" and "known."

**Pushback:** delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry (i.e., a *seller* knowledge qualifier on specific warranties), and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or the Ironquay/any specific indemnity.

## 6. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

Update says the consent "is addressed" via reasonable endeavours, deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms: ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), change-control clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3, **no final written consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied**.

A customer representing roughly 30% of revenue is material to valuation. "Reasonable endeavours" is insufficient and "consent-on-delivery" ignores the 11.3 conditions – a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is not an effective consent.

**Pushback:** Condition Precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent in agreed form and (b) evidence of satisfaction of 11.3 conditions, both before Completion. Seller obligation should be all reasonable endeavours with specific steps, plus a Buyer walk right if not satisfied by the long-stop date. Consider price protection if Bluefen's terms change.

## 7. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

Update: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge, and notes change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.

On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a post-completion release means we would own a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a potential change-of-control default on day one.

**Pushback:** current payout letter from Riverlark; direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed security releases (PPSR discharges, release deeds) delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval – neither exists.

## 8. Employee bonuses (DD-005) and funds flow

Update: AUD 420,000 completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised." Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are **not in the funds flow** and does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.

Bonuses triggered by Completion are a Completion-caused liability that will sit in the Company (our Company) post-Completion unless dealt with. "A matter for the Seller" is a statement of intent, not a mechanism.

**Pushback:** specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 **plus** triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accrual impacts) either paid by Seller at Completion or deducted from price as a Transaction Expense / Debt-like item. Request the on-cost calculation now. Confirm the continued-employment condition mechanics so that liability does not fall on us later.

## 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

Update: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the VDR.

The risk is not merely the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until paid. A payment-only indemnity does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, or the cost of remediating/re-procuring.

**Pushback:** broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from non-ownership/defective title to Ironquay deliverables, infringement claims and remediation, while preserving the SOW3 cure (pay the outstanding fees and obtain confirmatory assignment pre-Completion, ideally as a Completion deliverable). Note the AUD 180k is unverified either way – obtain bank evidence and Ironquay confirmation. Indemnity outside the general cap/basket/knowledge bar.

## 10. Export/privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

Update: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." Disclosure Letter para 6: download link sent to an unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); not established whether accessed, exact scope, or whether notification required; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.

Both sides are consistent that nothing is confirmed. Per playbook, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand – but "not expected to be material" is a Seller assertion, not a finding, and should not be adopted.

**Pushback:** covenant to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed/revoked), and provide updates through to Completion; a specific warranty on the incident as described; and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party), outside the general cap. Do not price it either way until facts are known.

## 11. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, AUD 330,000)

Update calls them ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 says the disclosure does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – so the Update's characterisation is unsupported by the Seller's own disclosure.

**Pushback:** no automatic Debt classification or price deduction (per playbook), but request renewal dates, terms, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-Completion. Then determine treatment in the working capital / debt-like definitions.

## 12. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"

Not agreed. Tax and IP remain OPEN. Folding them into a 20% / 18-month general regime would be a major concession by silence.

**Pushback:** reserve both expressly; separate Tax regime (and Tax indemnity) and IP regime to be negotiated. Do not accept unlimited liability language either – hold the position open.

## 13. Title evidence (DD-012)

Seller: title "is evidenced by the Company share register." Disclosure Letter para 10 itself concedes this is the source the Seller relies on and that Buyer verification is not done.

The share register is a Company-maintained internal document supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof.

**Pushback:** independent ASIC extracts and historical company search, review of the register against share certificates, transfer forms and board minutes, PPSR search over the shares and Seller, Seller constitutional/authority documents and board resolutions, and a legal opinion or officer's certificate on capacity. Fundamental warranties (section 2) backstop this.

## 14. Minor items noted in the Disclosure Letter

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, not landlord consent – acceptable, but make the notification a Seller pre-Completion covenant and get the lease to confirm no CoC default.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction, not triggered by a share sale on its face – confirm there is no change-of-control provision elsewhere in the contract before accepting.
- **Para 1.4 (no admissions):** fine as boilerplate, but combined with general disclosure it means the Seller discloses documents without disclosing their consequences – reinforces the need for specific fair disclosure.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the limitation package** – re-propose 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket, 24-month period. Do not treat the Seller's 20% and 18 months as acceptable absent Amelia Frost's written authority (none exists).
2. **Reinstate separate regimes** – Fundamental/Title (100%, 6+ years, no basket/knowledge bar), Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and covenant claims; delete the "limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default.
3. **Insert fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause.
4. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure**; delete data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
5. **Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion**; any residual qualifier is seller-knowledge-based, named persons, reasonable enquiry, never applying to title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.
6. **Bluefen** – effective consent plus evidence of satisfied 11.3 conditions as a CP; reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery rejected.
7. **Riverlark** – payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; no post-completion release without irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
8. **Bonuses** – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded; obtain on-cost figures.
9. **Ironquay** – broaden indemnity to ownership/infringement/remediation, keep the SOW3 cure, verify the AUD 180,000 independently, require confirmatory assignment pre-Completion.
10. **DD-006 incident** – preservation, investigation, update and specific indemnity covenants; do not adopt "not material" or assume breach.
11. **Sandbar** – request facts; no automatic Debt treatment or deduction.
12. **Title** – independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.
13. **Tax/IP** – expressly reserved as open; no acceptance of the general regime.

**Escalation:** Items 1 (cap/period fallbacks) and 7 (any post-completion Riverlark release) require Amelia Frost's written sign-off before any movement. Everything else can be marked up by the deal team within existing playbook authority.

**Pushback:** covenant to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed/revoked), and provide updates through to Completion; a specific warranty on the incident as described; and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party), outside the general cap. Do not price it either way until facts are known.

## 11. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, AUD 330,000)

Update calls them ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 says the disclosure does **not** state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – so the Update's characterisation is unsupported by the Seller's own disclosure.

**Pushback:** no automatic Debt classification or price deduction (per playbook), but request renewal dates, terms, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-Completion. Then determine treatment in the working capital / debt-like definitions.

## 12. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"

Not agreed. Tax and IP remain OPEN. Folding them into a 20% / 18-month general regime would be a major concession by silence.

**Pushback:** reserve both expressly; separate Tax regime (and Tax indemnity) and IP regime to be negotiated. Do not accept unlimited liability language either – hold the position open.

## 13. Title evidence (DD-012)

Seller: title "is evidenced by the Company share register." Disclosure Letter para 10 itself concedes this is the source the Seller relies on and that Buyer verification is not done.

The share register is a Company-maintained internal document supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof.

**Pushback:** independent ASIC extracts and historical company search, review of the register against share certificates, transfer forms and board minutes, PPSR search over the shares and Seller, Seller constitutional/authority documents and board resolutions, and a legal opinion or officer's certificate on capacity. Fundamental warranties (section 2) backstop this.

## 14. Minor items noted in the Disclosure Letter

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, not landlord consent – acceptable, but make the notification a Seller pre-Completion covenant and get the lease to confirm no CoC default.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction, not triggered by a share sale on its face – confirm there is no change-of-control provision elsewhere in the contract before accepting.
- **Para 1.4 (no admissions):** fine as boilerplate, but combined with general disclosure it means the Seller discloses documents without disclosing their consequences – reinforces the need for specific fair disclosure.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the limitation package** – re-propose 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket, 24-month period. Do not treat the Seller's 20% and 18 months as acceptable absent Amelia Frost's written authority (none exists).
2. **Reinstate separate regimes** – Fundamental/Title (100%, 6+ years, no basket/knowledge bar), Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and covenant claims; delete the "limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default.
3. **Insert fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause.
4. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure**; delete data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
5. **Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion**; any residual qualifier is seller-knowledge-based, named persons, reasonable enquiry, never applying to title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.
6. **Bluefen** – effective consent plus evidence of satisfied 11.3 conditions as a CP; reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery rejected.
7. **Riverlark** – payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; no post-completion release without irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
8. **Bonuses** – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded; obtain on-cost figures.
9. **Ironquay** – broaden indemnity to ownership/infringement/remediation, keep the SOW3 cure, verify the AUD 180,000 independently, require confirmatory assignment pre-Completion.
10. **DD-006 incident** – preservation, investigation, update and specific indemnity covenants; do not adopt "not material" or assume breach.
11. **Sandbar** – request facts; no automatic Debt treatment or deduction.
12. **Title** – independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.
13. **Tax/IP** – expressly reserved as open; no acceptance of the general regime.

**Escalation:** Items 1 (cap/period fallbacks) and 7 (any post-completion Riverlark release) require Amelia Frost's written sign-off before any movement. Everything else can be marked up by the deal team within existing playbook authority.
